record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given an undirected graph G with two distinguished vertices v1 and v2 and a positive integer k, does player one have a winning strategy in Generalized Hex that wins within at most k moves, where players alternately place white and black pebbles on unoccupied vertices and player one wins by creating a white path from v1 to v2?

evidence.quote: Question: Does player one have a winning strategy of at most k moves in Generalized Hex?
To the best of our knowledge, the problem remains open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Generalized Hex is the following two-player game. Given an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ with two distinguished vertices $v_1, v_2 \in V$, players alternate turns (Player 1 moves first). On each turn, the active player places a pebble of her color (Player 1 places white pebbles, Player 2 places black pebbles) on a vertex that is currently unoccupied. Player 1 wins as soon as the set of white-occupied vertices contains a path in $G$ from $v_1$ to $v_2$; otherwise Player 2 wins.

The Short Generalized Hex problem is: given $(G, v_1, v_2, k)$ where $k$ is a positive integer, decide whether Player 1 has a strategy that guarantees a win within at most $k$ of her own moves.

Determine the parameterized complexity of Short Generalized Hex when parameterized by $k$: is it fixed-parameter tractable, and if not, classify it within the W-hierarchy or AW-hierarchy.
artifact.status_search_result: The parameterized complexity of Short Generalized Hex was resolved by Bonnet, Gaspers, Lambilliotte, Rümmele, and Saffidine in "The Parameterized Complexity of Positional Games" (ICALP 2017, arXiv:1704.08536). They proved that Short Generalized Hex is W[1]-complete when parameterized by the number of moves, settling the open question from the Downey–Fellows list.

status_evidence.title: The Parameterized Complexity of Positional Games
status_evidence.snippet: Short Generalized Hex is W[1]-complete parameterized by the number of moves. This solves an open problem from Downey and Fellows' influential list of open problems from 1999.
status_evidence.claim: Short Generalized Hex is W[1]-complete parameterized by number of moves, resolving the Downey–Fellows open problem.

status_evidence.title: The Parameterized Complexity of Positional Games (DROPS/ICALP 2017)
status_evidence.snippet: Bonnet, Gaspers, Lambilliotte, Rümmele, Saffidine — ICALP 2017 proceedings establishing W[1]-completeness of Short Generalized Hex.
status_evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed ICALP 2017 publication of the W[1]-completeness result.
